name: Submagic
tagline: Browser tool that auto-captions, trims and dresses up vertical short-form video with animated subtitles, b-roll and effects.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The technical core is not a secret: Whisper gives you word-level timestamps, ffmpeg with libass burns karaoke-style captions, and a coding agent can wire that into a script in an afternoon. What you cannot one-shot is the taste layer: dozens of tuned caption templates, emoji placement that lands on the right word, auto zoom cuts, b-roll that matches what was said, and a render farm that returns a finished vertical video in a minute instead of ten. If you post one style of video and want burned-in animated captions, the local build genuinely replaces the subscription. If you are shipping daily clips for clients and picking a look per video, you are paying for the templates and the render speed, not the transcription.
coreLoopDIY: Transcribes a video locally with word-level timestamps, generates an animated ASS subtitle file in a chosen preset style, and burns it into a vertical export with ffmpeg.
requirements: Python 3.11 and faster-whisper (runs on CPU, much faster with a GPU)
a few GB of disk for model weights
fonts installed locally for the caption styles
whatYouLose: The template gallery: dozens of caption looks that already read well on phone screens
Auto b-roll, stock footage matching and AI sound effects
Auto zoom, silence removal and highlight clip detection tuned for retention
Cloud rendering, so long videos tie up your own machine
Multi-language translation and dubbing in one click, plus a shareable web editor for clients
moatNotes: The moat is aesthetic defaults plus render latency. Both are real, neither is patentable.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the difference between a caption file and a caption that looks good is a hundred small decisions about font weight, stroke, vertical position, word grouping and highlight timing, and Submagic has already made them for you in a dozen flavors. Volume creators are also buying throughput: uploading, picking a preset and getting back a rendered file while they do something else beats babysitting a local ffmpeg job. The local build wins if you have exactly one look you like and enough patience to tune it once.
notes: Transcription is commodity, caption taste is not, and you can borrow taste by copying one template you like and never changing it.
prompt:
Build a local command line tool called "clipcap" that burns animated word-by-word captions into short vertical videos. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non negotiable:
- Python 3.11, single package, dependencies managed with uv
- faster-whisper for transcription with word level timestamps
- ffmpeg (must be on PATH, with libass) for all video work
- typer for the CLI, rich for progress output

Commands:
1. `clipcap caption INPUT.mp4 --style bold-yellow --out OUT.mp4`
   - extract audio to 16k mono wav with ffmpeg
   - transcribe with faster-whisper, model configurable via .env (default "small"), word_timestamps=True
   - cache the transcript as INPUT.words.json so re-renders skip transcription
   - group words into caption lines of at most 3 words or 1.2 seconds
   - emit an .ass subtitle file where the currently spoken word is highlighted using per-word \k karaoke timing plus an inline color override
   - burn in with `ffmpeg -vf ass=...`, copy audio, output h264 yuv420p
2. `clipcap crop INPUT.mp4 --out OUT.mp4` : center crop to 9:16, scale to 1080x1920
3. `clipcap styles` : list available presets
4. `clipcap edit INPUT.words.json` : open the transcript in $EDITOR so typos can be fixed before rendering

Styles live in styles/*.toml with font, size, primary color, highlight color, outline width, shadow, vertical margin, uppercase bool. Ship exactly three presets: bold-yellow, clean-white, karaoke-green. Validate that the font resolves and fail loudly if not.

Out of scope, do not build: b-roll insertion, stock footage, emoji generation, auto zoom, silence trimming, translation, any web UI, any API server.

Deliverables: pyproject.toml, README with a 60 second quickstart, .env.example with WHISPER_MODEL and WHISPER_DEVICE, and one sample invocation that works end to end on a 30 second test clip you generate with ffmpeg's testsrc plus a spoken audio file the user supplies. Exit codes non zero on failure, no silent fallbacks.
